s: A solutions architect is designing an application to accept timesheet entries from employees on their mobile devices. Timesheets will be submitted weekly, with most of the submissions occurring on Friday. The data must be stored in a format that allows payroll administrators to run monthly reports The infrastructure must be highly available and scale to match the rate of incoming data and reporting requests. Which combination of steps meets these requirements while minimizing operational overhead? (Select TWO}
o: Deploy the application to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances with load balancing across multiple Availability Zones. Use scheduled Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to add capacity before the high volume of submissions on Fridays

Deploy the application in a container using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with load balancing across multiple Availability Zones Use scheduled Service Auto Scaling to add capacity before the high volume of submissions on Fridays
Deploy the application front end to an Amazon S3 bucket served by Amazon CloudFront Deploy the application backend using Amazon API Gateway with an AWS Lambda proxy integration
Store the timesheet submission data in Amazon Redshift Use Amazon QuickSight to generate the reports using Amazon Redshift as the data source
Store the timesheet submission data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena and Amazon QuickSight to generate the reports using Amazon S3 as the data source.

w.y: Minimizing operational overhead points to serverless for both parts. An S3 plus CloudFront front end with an API Gateway and Lambda backend is highly available and scales automatically with the Friday spike, with no capacity planning. Storing the submissions in S3 and querying them with Athena and QuickSight gives serverless monthly reporting.

o.A: EC2 instances with scheduled scaling mean managing servers and guessing capacity.
o.B: ECS still requires cluster and scaling management, and scheduled scaling can miss off-schedule spikes.
o.C: Correct: a static front end on S3 and CloudFront with an API Gateway and Lambda backend scales automatically and needs no servers.
o.D: Redshift is a provisioned data warehouse with more cost and management than weekly timesheets justify.
o.E: Correct: S3 is cheap, durable storage, and Athena with QuickSight gives serverless reports on demand.
